overview: A tech- and markets-heavy day. NVIDIA researchers released Sigma, the first large-scale (3B/8B) continuous diffusion language model, and Burry Tracker reported Michael Burry's case that Nvidia overstates how well its old chips hold value. Smaller items include the CFTC opening public comment on crypto rules, Google's AI-for-science roundup, and Starlink spreading across United's fleet. Much of the feed was politics, which is skipped here.

top_items.title: burrytracker - Burry argues Nvidia's chip resale claims rest on rental estimates; he holds Sept 2027 $NVDA puts with calls as a hedge
zhihanyang_ - NVIDIA team presents Sigma, a 3B/8B continuous diffusion LM said to match discrete diffusion and AR models on math and code
brian_armstrong - Coinbase CEO praises the CFTC for opening a public comment period on its crypto rulemaking
demishassabis - Google's AI-for-science push includes AlphaGenome Atlas, which maps all 9B single-letter genome changes, and WeatherNext 3
burrytracker - Burry's MercadoLibre position is up 11.5% after 150 days, with Brazil rallying on Bolsonaro's election lead
tobi - Shopify CEO says he's hearing many stories of shoppers using Muse to buy direct from brands instead of Amazon
chamath - Endorses Nadella's point that companies renting closed AI models 'pay for intelligence twice': in money and in leaked know-how
